subject: Recap & DPA/SCC path — Novus Retail compliance items
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Strand <oliver.strand@novusretail.com>
Cc: security@novusretail.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00Z
Subject: Recap & DPA/SCC path — Novus Retail compliance items

Hi Oliver — great to meet this morning. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment before legal does a deeper pass.

Summary of what we covered:
- Use case: product search re-ranking + personalized recommendations; low-latency inference in US regions.
- Data scope: customer product catalog + hashed user behavior (no raw PII expected in payloads).
- Compliance expectations: SOC 2 in-scope, GDPR DPA with SCCs for EU data in the future, potential HIPAA considerations if you expand into healthcare vertical.

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Please send your vendor security questionnaire (attached is our vendor SQ for reference).
2) Confirm whether Novus will be a controller or processor for the primary product feed — you mentioned the catalog is controller-owned, please confirm for contractual mapping.
3) Any hard deadlines for contract signature / procurement? you mentioned kickoff target mid-November.

What we’ll do next:
- Share our SOC 2 summary and the DPA draft with SCC options for your review (attached).
- Loop in our legal and security leads for the vendor questionnaire and controller/processor mapping.
- Propose a short follow-up call next week to walk through the questionnaire answers.

Attachments: vendor_security_questionnaire_v1.pdf (our SQ), redwood-soc2-summary-2026.pdf (summary).

Thanks — I’ll copy Neha (legal) and Dev (solutions) on the follow-up.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0123

Subject: Re: Recap & DPA/SCC path — Novus Retail compliance items

Thanks Sean — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick clarifications: 

- Confirming Novus treats the product catalog as controller-owned; for behavioral signals we need to verify how identifiers are passed but assume controller as well unless we contract otherwise.
- Procurement timeline: procurement needs a signed agreement by 2026-11-15 to hit the launch window.
- I attached our baseline vendor security questionnaire (will upload to your drive link) — it’s fairly standard but includes a short section on SCC modules which our legal prefers to see spelled out in the DPA.

I’ll schedule a 30 min follow-up for next Tuesday. In the meantime, please have your legal take a look at which SCC module(s) you propose and whether Redwood intends to act as processor for the EU data flows.

Oliver

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T08:17:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Recap & DPA/SCC path — Novus Retail compliance items

Neha / Dev — forwarding Oliver’s reply and Novus’ vendor SQ. Key asks from them: 1) confirm controller/processor stance for both catalog + behavioral signals, 2) propose SCC module(s) for the DPA, and 3) confirm we can hit procurement timeline (11/15).

Notes: from a product angle we typically process tokenized/hashed behavioral events and do not store raw contact PII; we should confirm whether that aligns with their definitions. Dev — can you draft a short technical paragraph describing data flows, what we persist, and how we segregate customer data (KV cache lifespan, retention defaults)?

Neha — can you propose SCC module language and confirm whether Redwood will sign as processor for the described flows? If you think controller/processor nuances could push procurement, flag items we can triage (e.g., addendum to limit categories of data).

I attached the vendor SQ and our SOC2 summary in the original thread — want to be ready for the Tuesday call.

Thanks,
Sean
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-05T15:44:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Recap & DPA/SCC path — Novus Retail compliance items

Hi team — quick legal take after an initial review of the SQ and notes below.

1) Controller / Processor: Based on Oliver’s characterization, Novus will be the controller and Redwood will be the processor for the catalog and behavioral signals. We should document this explicitly in the DPA (processor annex). If Novus wants to treat Redwood as a joint controller for any analytics work, that will need additional scoping language — flag that if they ask.

2) SCC module selection: recommend offering Module Two (Controller-to-Processor) where applicable and Module Three where we host/transfer data to subprocessors in other jurisdictions. Provide Novus the option to select the modules in the DPA template — we should not pre-select a single module without confirming their legal team’s preference.

3) DPA draft & timeline: I’ll prepare a DPA draft with SCC module options and a short processor annex describing typical data flows. That should be ready for internal review by EOD Monday 2026-10-06. If procurement needs signed agreement by 2026-11-15, we have runway, but we should avoid extended redlines on data residency / subprocessors.

4) SOC 2 evidence: we can share the SOC2 summary now and provide report under NDA if requested. For RFP items that require attestation, note that SOC2 type II for 2026 is in-scope but full report release requires an executed NDA / customer request.

Attachments: none.

Next steps: I will upload the DPA draft to the Drive link and drop proposed SCC wording. Dev — please send the short technical data-flow paragraph and retention defaults so I can include it in the processor annex.

-Neha
General Counsel (Contracts) — Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
